attack_mechanism: A transient or persistent fault on `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.dscratch0` during CSR update or request issue can flip the effective privilege used for that load/store. For a load or store issued while `mstatus_mprv = 1`, the control unit assigns `ctrl_o.lsu_priv <= csr.mstatus_mpp`. `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.dscratch0` can alter the CSR write, trap/debug return, or stored `mstatus_mpp` value used by that MPRV branch; the relevant assignment conditions include `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.csr_re`, `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.rf_rs2`, `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.alu_opb_mux`, `neorv32_cpu.ctrl.alu_sub`, and the remaining path guards. The candidate and asset are linked by `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.dscratch0 -> neorv32_cpu.csr_rdata -> neorv32_cpu.alu_add -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. The LSU request metadata carries an unintended effective privilege, allowing a memory access to be checked as a more privileged operation.

The candidate and asset are linked by `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.dscratch0 -> neorv32_cpu.csr_rdata -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr_wdata -> neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. The LSU selects the wrong privilege source and applies an unintended protection domain to the pending memory request.
